s: Which of the following best describes the Right to Be Forgotten (RTBF)?
o: Removal, masking or de-indexing of outdated, irrelevant or harmful personal information
A right available only to government employees
Permanent deletion of every judicial record concerning a person
A right to prevent all forms of online identification
x: RTBF concerns the removal, masking or de-indexing of outdated, irrelevant or harmful personal information. It does not require the deletion of every judicial record.
tq: Identify the exact scope of the right instead of choosing an extreme formulation.
sec: Global frameworks - EU GDPR, right to erasure, right to be forgotten

s: Under which provision of the GDPR was the Right to Be Forgotten formalised as the Right to Erasure?

tq: Discriminate between closely related article and section numbers.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Be Forgotten in India:
1. It forms part of the right to privacy under Article 21.
2. It is an absolute right applicable without any limitation.
3. It does not erase judicial records but may limit name-based searches.
4. Section 12 of the DPDP Act provides a Right to Erasure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the right is not absolute; it does not erase judicial records and may operate by limiting name-based searches.
tq: Find the statement that improperly converts a qualified right into an absolute one.
sec: Global frameworks - EU GDPR, right to erasure, right to be forgotten

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Right to Be Forgotten from a general deletion of judicial records?
o: It applies only to biometric data collected by UIDAI.
It automatically cancels the judgment of a court.
It prohibits every search involving the person’s name.
It limits name-based searches without necessarily erasing judicial records.
x: The Indian understanding of RTBF does not erase judicial records; it can limit name-based searches in appropriate circumstances.
tq: Separate de-indexing or search limitation from destruction of the underlying record.
sec: Global frameworks - EU GDPR, right to erasure, right to be forgotten

Gobind v State of Madhya Pradesh

tq: Use the case-specific association rather than the broader constitutional source of privacy.
sec: Global frameworks - EU GDPR, right to erasure, right to be forgotten

s:
With reference to litigation concerning the DPDP Act and the RTI Act, consider the following pairs:
1. Venkatesh Nayak — petition before a three-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant
2. Constitution Bench — reference of challenges to the amendment
3. Geeta Seshu and SFLC — plea concerning personal data and public data
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The litigation includes the Venkatesh Nayak petition, reference of challenges to a Constitution Bench, and the plea by Geeta Seshu and SFLC on personal data versus public data.
tq: Start with the sure person–litigation pair and verify the institutional details.
sec: RTI-privacy debate - amendment to Section 8(1)(j)

s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. The Supreme Court asked whether the law was ‘crippling RTI’.
B. A three-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant heard the Venkatesh Nayak petition.
C. Challenges were referred to a Constitution Bench.
D. The Supreme Court considered a plea concerning ‘personal data’ and ‘public data’ by Geeta Seshu and SFLC.
x: The sequence was 15 February 2026, 25 February 2026, 13 March 2026 and 8 August 2026 respectively.
tq: Use the dates to fix the first and last events before ordering the middle events.
sec: RTI-privacy debate - amendment to Section 8(1)(j)

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the DPDP Act’s exemptions or exclusions?
o: Notified State agencies — possible exemption on grounds of sovereignty, security or public order
x: Journalism receives no exemption. Notified State agencies, research, archiving, statistics and potentially startups are the categories referred to for exemptions.
tq: Find the exception by distinguishing a possible exemption from the expressly excluded category.
sec: RTI-privacy debate - amendment to Section 8(1)(j)

s: Which provision of the DPDP Act permits the State to process personal data without obtaining consent in specified circumstances?
x: Section 7, dealing with ‘legitimate uses’, allows the State to process data without consent.
tq: Match the statutory section with the function it performs.
sec: RTI-privacy debate - amendment to Section 8(1)(j)

s: Pegasus spyware is best described as which of the following?
o: A zero-click spyware developed by NSO Group
A statutory interception mechanism under the Telecommunications Act
A facial-recognition database operated by the Delhi Police
x: Pegasus is a zero-click spyware associated with the NSO Group.
tq: Use the exact technical description to distinguish spyware from surveillance laws and databases.
sec: Surveillance and privacy - Pegasus inquiry, interception provisions

s: The Supreme Court-appointed technical committee in the Pegasus matter was supervised by:
x: The technical committee was supervised by Justice R.V. Raveendran.
tq: Apply the wrong-person trap to distinguish the supervising judge from other judicial figures.
sec: Surveillance and privacy - Pegasus inquiry, interception provisions

s: Which of the following correctly describes the finding of the Supreme Court-appointed technical committee in the Pegasus matter?
o: Malware was found on five of 29 phones, but it could not be conclusively linked to Pegasus.
The committee conclusively established that Pegasus had been used by a particular government agency.
Pegasus was conclusively found on all 29 phones examined.
No malware was found on any of the phones examined.
x: The committee found malware on five of the 29 phones examined, but could not conclusively establish that it was Pegasus.
tq: Separate the numerical finding from the stronger but unsupported claim of conclusive attribution.
sec: Surveillance and privacy - Pegasus inquiry, interception provisions

s: Which of the following legal combinations is associated with interception of communications in India?
o: Section 69 of the IT Act and Section 5(2) of the Telegraph Act, now under the Telecommunications Act, 2023
Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act and Section 17 of the DPDP Act
Section 7 of the DPDP Act and the Constitution Bench procedure
The GDPR and the Telecommunications Act, 1885
x: Interception is associated with Section 69 of the IT Act and Section 5(2) of the Telegraph Act, 1885, with the latter framework now under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
tq: Match each interception provision with its correct statute and legislative successor.
sec: Surveillance and privacy - Pegasus inquiry, interception provisions

s: The safeguards governing interception, referred to in the context of privacy protection, were laid down in:
o: Laksh Vir Singh Yadav v Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
Puttaswamy v Union of India, 2017 only
x: The relevant safeguards for interception were laid down in PUCL v Union of India in 1997.
tq: Use the case-name and year pair to avoid confusing interception safeguards with broader privacy judgments.
sec: Surveillance and privacy - Pegasus inquiry, interception provisions

s:
Consider the following statements regarding facial-recognition surveillance:
1. A Member of Parliament approached the Supreme Court against the Delhi Police’s use of facial-recognition technology during NEET-UG protests.
2. The National Automated Facial Recognition System operates without a specific statute.
3. State surveillance must satisfy the tests laid down in Puttaswamy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The challenge concerned Delhi Police use during NEET-UG protests, NAFRS operates without a statute, and surveillance must meet the Puttaswamy tests.
tq: Check each statement independently, especially the statutory-status statement containing ‘without’.
sec: Surveillance and privacy - Pegasus inquiry, interception provisions

s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised right of a Data Principal under the DPDP framework?
o: Right to impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary
x: The listed rights include information and access, correction, erasure, grievance redress, withdrawal of consent and nomination. A Data Principal does not impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary.
tq: Identify the outsider by separating an individual data right from an enforcement power.
sec: Rights and duties of Data Principals  [GROUP-II]

s: Which of the following is a duty of a Data Principal?
o: To avoid furnishing false information or impersonating another person
To appoint the Data Protection Board
To exempt startups from the DPDP Act
To provide only verified parental consent for every adult’s data
x: A Data Principal must not provide false information or impersonate another person. Avoiding frivolous complaints is another stated duty.
tq: Translate the statutory duty into a practical conduct-based situation.
sec: Rights and duties of Data Principals  [GROUP-II]

s: In relation to processing the personal data of children, which one of the following is correct?
o: Verifiable parental consent is required for persons below 18 years of age.
Consent is required only for targeted advertisements, not for processing data.
Only written consent from the school is required.
Parental consent is unnecessary if the child is above 16 years of age.
x: The framework requires verifiable parental consent for persons under 18 years of age.
tq: Use the age threshold to distinguish children’s-data consent from adult consent.
sec: Children's data - consent and tracking  [GROUP-II]

s: Which of the following activities is prohibited when aimed at children under the DPDP framework?
o: Processing under legitimate uses by the State
Tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising
x: Tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertisements aimed at children are prohibited.
tq: Find the prohibited conduct by grouping the child-protection restrictions together.
sec: Children's data - consent and tracking  [GROUP-II]

s: The penalty mentioned for a breach relating to children’s data is up to:
x: A breach relating to children’s data may attract a penalty of up to ₹200 crore.
tq: Compare the numerical penalty with the separate ₹10,000 duty-related penalty.
sec: Children's data - consent and tracking  [GROUP-II]

s: In Laksh Vir Singh Yadav v Union of India, the Delhi High Court dealt with which issue?
o: Interception under Section 69 of the IT Act
Exemption of startups from data protection obligations
De-indexing name-based search results for acquitted persons
Appointment of the Data Protection Board
x: The Delhi High Court laid down a framework for de-indexing name-based results concerning persons who had been acquitted.
tq: Match the case with its distinctive remedy rather than with a general privacy principle.
sec: Universal angles

s: The rules relating to Consent Managers were expected by which month and year?
x: Consent Manager rules were due in November 2026.
tq: Read the deadline precisely and distinguish it from the publication date of the forecast.
sec: Universal angles

s:
Consider the following criticisms and debates concerning the DPDP framework:
1. Broad exemptions for the State
2. Absence of data portability
3. Questions concerning Board independence
4. Dilution of RTI through Section 44(3)
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four are identified criticisms or areas of debate concerning the DPDP framework.
tq: Test a complete list by checking whether the final item is also included rather than stopping at the familiar first three.
sec: Universal angles

s: The AP Police AI4AP pilot referred to in the context of DPDP compliance is being undertaken in which districts?
x: The AI4AP pilot is associated with Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya, and raises DPDP compliance issues.
tq: Use the location-list distinction to identify the exact districts involved in the pilot.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following is linked to the DPDP Act in the context of current national standards?
o: Standards on cloud, data centres and ethical artificial intelligence
Standards only on agricultural markets and crop insurance
x: National standards on cloud services, data centres and ethical AI are linked to the DPDP Act.
tq: Connect the broad technology-governance domains with the data-protection framework.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which statement best describes the comparative position of the DPDP framework vis-à-vis the GDPR?
o: The DPDP framework is broader, more detailed and primarily criminal-penalty based.
The DPDP framework is narrower, lighter and based on financial penalties.
The DPDP framework excludes all financial penalties and relies only on data portability.
The two frameworks are identical in scope and enforcement.
x: The DPDP framework is described as narrower and lighter than the GDPR, with a financial-penalty-based enforcement approach.
tq: Test all three comparison dimensions—scope, regulatory weight and penalty model—together.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following issues is specifically included among the debates concerning journalists and the DPDP framework?
o: Journalists being treated as Data Fiduciaries
Journalists being made members of the Consent Manager authority
Journalists being prohibited from filing RTI applications
Journalists receiving an automatic exemption from all obligations
x: The debates include the treatment of journalists as ‘Data Fiduciaries’; journalism does not receive a general exemption.
tq: Distinguish the debated classification of journalists from the separate question of exemption.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following correctly identifies the status of the Supreme Court’s DPDP–RTI proceedings mentioned for August 2026?
o: The challenge concerned only children’s targeted advertising.
The Supreme Court had dismissed the challenge without examination.
The matter had been transferred exclusively to the Delhi High Court.
The Supreme Court was hearing the challenge concerning the DPDP Act and RTI.
x: The Supreme Court was hearing the challenge to the interaction between the DPDP Act and the RTI framework in August 2026.
tq: Distinguish an ongoing hearing from a final judicial determination.
sec: Universal angles
